features.notes: Moved out of engines.load_and_simulate by #8618: the tile is a club-design workbench, not an engine load/simulate surface, and the two launcher tiles (bunkershot3d -> a notebook script, bunker_shot -> the GUI) were reconciled into this one entry point. The computation lives in src/tools/bunker_shot_gui/model.py, which imports no GUI toolkit and is the layer a React port would consume; no API route or web page exists yet. The visualization suite (epic #8699) keeps that split: shot3d.py and traces.py compute, render3d.py and render_traces.py draw headlessly through matplotlib, and viewport_widgets.py only wires them to a canvas. A React port would consume shot3d.viewport_payload, which is the backend-neutral ADR-0027 ViewportOverlayPayload and carries the envelope status and fidelity tier in its metadata so any renderer can stamp its own frames. The F1 sand cut (#8710, #8711) keeps the same split and adds one constraint a port must honour: the field carries its fidelity tier and validity status as data covered by a SHA-256 over the provenance and the arrays together, so any client that renders a field must read the standing out of the file rather than out of its filename, and must refuse a field whose digest does not match.
